### Analysis

This report describes `extra_streamlit_components.CookieManager` (a third-party custom component) failing to load when Streamlit is mounted alongside a FastAPI app and served via `uvicorn`. The issue body provides **no reproducible code, no steps to reproduce, no error message/traceback, and no environment info** (Streamlit version, Python version, OS, browser), so the cause cannot be confirmed.

Streamlit is officially served by its own Tornado-based server (`streamlit run`); mounting Streamlit into a FastAPI/ASGI app under `uvicorn` is not a supported deployment pattern (see #4311). When attempted, custom components typically fail because their static assets (HTML/JS bundles) are served by Streamlit's `ComponentRequestHandler` from `/component/<name>/...` routes — when Streamlit is mounted under a sub-path or proxied through another ASGI app, these routes (and the WebSocket / XSRF cookie flow that components rely on) frequently break, which is the most likely root cause here.

Recommendation: request a minimal reproduction, the exact error/console output, and version info, and treat this as a third-party/unsupported-deployment question rather than a defect in Streamlit core.

### Related Issues

- [#4311 — Provide way to run with the WSGI/ASGI protocols](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/4311): Tracks the request to support uvicorn/ASGI deployments. Directly relevant: running Streamlit under uvicorn is the unsupported scenario described here.
- [#4567 — Integration with Flask - render simple Streamlit component on Flask or Fast API](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/4567): Tracks embedding/mounting Streamlit components into Flask/FastAPI — the exact setup described in this report.
- [#861 — Ability to write cookies](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues/861): The long-standing request for native cookie support; users adopt `extra_streamlit_components.CookieManager` as a workaround, so progress here would reduce dependence on the failing third-party component.
